# #2050: Patch: classify counts a `use`-only change in a non-script Rust file as a code change
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a pull request only moves code between files — a function moves from one module to another, so one file's `use` lines change and nothing else does — the tool that decides "did game behaviour change?" reports "no". CI then skips its deeper check and passes the PR as an internal change even if the move changed which code actually runs. After this patch an import-only change in engine, cards or AI source still counts as a code change and gets the full check.

## Why

`classify::code_changed` (`crates/tools/src/classify.rs:212-221`) runs `catalog::code_lines` on every `.rs` path; `code_lines` (`crates/tools/src/catalog.rs:1732-1841`) strips `use` declarations and everything at or below `#[cfg(test)]` — right for counting a card script's LOC (the `Area::Script` case), wrong for `crates/engine/src/`, `crates/cards/src/` non-scripts and `crates/ai/src/` (`area()`, classify.rs:166-208). A use-only diff leaves `play_code`/`ai` unset, `unchecked` stays empty (classify.rs:399-407), CI's `rust (classify)` never builds or runs stage 2, and `--claims` passes a genuine behaviour change as `kind:internal` — exactly the gap the claims check exists to close (R1370000).

## Proposal

Keep the LOC normalizer for `Area::Script` paths; for non-script `.rs` paths use a second normalizer that keeps `use` lines (still dropping comments and test modules). Fold in a small adjacent fix: assert each `AI_TOOLING` entry (classify.rs:57) names a real file, so a rename can't leave a dead entry and a spurious `Area::Ai`.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/classify.rs` (and `catalog.rs` if the second normalizer lives there), `crates/tools/tests/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `use`-only diff in `crates/engine/src/` or `crates/ai/src/` marks its area changed and triggers stage 2
- [ ] A `use`-only diff in a card script still reports no LOC change
- [ ] Comment-only and test-only diffs still count as no code change
- [ ] `AI_TOOLING` entries are checked against real files

## Size and risks

Small-medium. Care is needed not to reclassify comment or test churn as code changes; the two-normalizer split keeps the LOC semantics intact where they are load-bearing (Area::Script, `catalog loc`).
